Strategic Roadmap and Action Plan 2023-2027 b
Preface
The first five years in the life of a new agency is like a light-year worth of distance in
space and time. It is within this period that formative actions are taken which continue
to echo through generations. The work of the Nigeria Data Protection Commission (the
Commission) will be preserved for posterity. It is with this full sense of responsibility
that the Commission resolved to craft a Strategic Roadmap and Action Plan (SRAP)
2023-2027.
Our institutional mandate rests on a rich framework of Data Protection and Privacy (DPP)
which consists of the 1999 Constitution of the Federal Republic of Nigeria; Nigeria Data
Protection Regulation (NDPR) 2019; Nigeria Data Protection Act (NDPA) 2023; United
Nations’ Universal Declaration of Human Rights 1948; the International Covenant
on Civil and Political Rights 1966; the ECOWAS Supplementary Act A/SA.1/01/10 on
Personal Data Protection within ECOWAS (Thirty-Seventh Session of The Authority of
Heads of State And Government); African Union Malabo Convention on Cyber Security
and Personal Data Protection 2014 (The Malabo Convention), Convention 108 +, and
other instruments.
The objectives of the NDPA particularly provided guidance in developing this SRAP.
They are to safeguard the fundamental rights, freedom and interests of data subjects,
as guaranteed under the Constitution of the Federal Republic of Nigeria, 1999 and
provide for the regulation of processing of personal data, amongst others - Section 1
of the NDPA.
Thus, the SRAP Committee was constituted on the 30th of March 2022 with terms of
reference rooted in the frameworks. The Committee engaged with experts within and
outside Nigeria, and the outcome of these efforts is the Strategic Roadmap and Action
Plan (SRAP) 2023-2027.
The work covers five pillars namely: Governance, Ecosystem and Technology, Capacity
Development, Cooperation and Collaboration, Funding and Sustainability. In each of
these pillars are time-bound activities and outcomes which are carefully crafted to
guide the Commission in the discharge of its mandate.
With SRAP (2023-2027), our work at the Commission has been cut out for us. We
believe that with the substantial implementation of this roadmap, we will have achieved
a trusted and sustainable ecosystem where the rights of data subjects are protected.
Dr. Vincent O. Olatunji, CPPPS, CDPO, FIIM
National Commissioner/ CEO
Nigeria Data Protection Commission
November 2023
Nigeria Data Protection Commission (NDPC) info@ndpc.gov.ng

Strategic Roadmap and Action Plan 2023-2027 c
Foreword
Data privacy occupies a central place in the Nigerian legal system. This, of course,
is a deduction that rests on the authority of our grund norm, 1999 Constitution of
the Federal Republic of Nigeria; which provides under section 37 thus: “The privacy
of citizens, their homes, correspondence, telephone conversations, and telegraphic
communications is hereby guaranteed and protected.”
On my assumption of duty as the Honorable Minister of Communications, Innovation
and Digital Economy, I developed the Strategic Blueprint for the sector in line
with President Bola Ahmed Tinubu’s Renewed Hope Agenda. The Blueprint is to
provide strategic direction for effective deployment of digital technologies to drive
Mr President’s 8-point agenda in line with the current trends of the 4th industrial
revolution.
On 12 June 2023, President Bola Ahmed Tinubu, GCFR, gave Presidential assent
to the Nigeria Data Protection Bill thus providing a principal legislation for data
protection in Nigeria which will further guarantee the rights of Nigerians and global
competitiveness of our businesses.
Life as we know it today increasingly depends on the digital space. Invariably, for us
to improve lives and livelihoods, we must chart a roadmap that enables the use of
data for improved well-being and sustainable development. In effect, our effort must
be a balancing act in which citizens can find sanctuary in the protective power of our
laws and institutions on the one hand, and fulfillment through the opportunities of the
data economy on the other hand.
The 5-pillars of our Strategic Blueprint served as a guide in crafting a Strategic Roadmap
and Action Plan (SRAP) 2023-2027 for the Nigeria Data Protection Commission
(NDPC) and the nascent Data Protection and Privacy (DPP) ecosystem in Nigeria.
It is obvious that the dynamics of the 4th Industrial Revolution and international comity
thrust upon us novel issues that may require contemporary innovations, we can rest
assured that the fundamentals of the SRAP (2023-2027) will remain a key reference
point of our regulatory actions in the days and years ahead.
I commit the Strategic Roadmap and Action Plan (SRAP) 2023-2027 to our
stakeholders and to our partners within our nation and the international community.
Dr ‘Bosun Tijani,
Honourable Minister of Communications,
Innovation & Digital Economy
Federal Republic of Nigeria
November 2023
Nigeria Data Protection Commission (NDPC) info@ndpc.gov.ng

Strategic Roadmap and Action Plan 2023-2027 d
Acknowledgment
The Nigeria Data Protection Strategic Roadmap and Action Plan (NDP-SRAP) 2023-
2027 provides essential guidance on executing a desired strategic direction, and the
current administration has expressed confidence in the Data Protection and Privacy
ecosystem’s ability to catalyse the anticipated change in the digital space. The SRAP
2023-2027 communicates the government’s commitment to delivering on its promise
of renewed hope using data and leveraging the digital environment to create jobs,
wealth, improve productivity and promote inclusive development.
The roadmap will benefit government agencies, civil societies, investors, operators,
consumers, partner organisations, professional groups, and other stakeholders. We
express our gratitude to the President of the Federal Republic of Nigeria, Bola Ahmed
Tinubu, GCFR, and his administration for their stewardship and support.
The committee appreciates the contributions of the National Information Technology
Development Agency, National Identity Management Commission, KPMG, Inssata
Ricourt, Aissatou Sylla, Samuel Ifeanyi Ngwu, Olumide Babalola, Muhiz Adisa, Tamar
Kaaldani, and European Commission’s project “International Digital Cooperation -
Enhanced Digital Cooperation and Data Flows”. We value the untiring efforts of the
National Commissioner/ CEO, Dr Vincent Olatunji; the management and staff of the
Nigeria Data Protection Commission (NDPC); and the secretariat team, consisting of
Babatunde Bamigboye, Leena Abba, Chiderah Ike-Okonkwo, and Hassan Olugbile.
I commend the professionalism and commitment of the SRAP 2023-2027 committee,
including Abdulaziz A. Aliyu, Ayoh O. A. Ogon, Emmanuel Edet, Ivan I. Anya, Jide Awe,
Nkemdilim Ilo, Segun H. Olugbile, Suwaiba Muhammad Dankabo, and Tunde Balogun,
for their contributions towards developing the roadmap.
Abdul-Hakeem Ajijola
Chairman, SRAP Committee
November, 2023

Strategic Roadmap and Action Plan 2023-2027 5
Conclusion
The successful implementation of the roadmap will result in a conducive environment
that ensures the trusted safe, reliable, and efficient utilisation of personal data.
This will nurture a thriving ecosystem that supports innovation geared at building trusted
systems and processes. It includes a data protection compliance partner ecosystem
that would lead to the emergence of a sustainable data protection ecosystem driven
primarily by people, supported by teaching, learning, research, and development.
The NDP-SRAP 2023-2027 ultimately sets out broad practical steps that government
intends to take towards deepening the culture of respect for privacy rights on the one
hand, and fostering beneficial and trusted use of data for sustainable development on
the other hand.

Conclusion
The National Data Protection Strategic Roadmap and Action Plan (NDP-SRAP) 2023
- 2027, is a set of measures designed to promote the growth and consolidation of a
sustainable and trustworthy Data Protection and Privacy (DPP) ecosystem in Nigeria as
well as provide strategic direction for the NDPC.
The NDP-SRAP is guided by its pillars: Governance; Ecosystem and Technology;
Capacity Development; Cooperation and Collaboration; Funding and
Sustainability, which outlines the direction and commitment to positioning the
ecosystem as a catalyst for sustainable development, optimizing opportunities, and
enhancing the well-being of Nigerian citizens.
By implementing this Roadmap, the aim is to build the momentum of the ecosystem’s
contribution to national economic growth and unlock new opportunities for greater
impact on the lives of our people.
